comment: The brain wire, version 2: the one protocol between a brain's driver (Go: apps/locus/keeper/internal/brainwire, which cmd/cyfr-claude-code and cmd/cyfr-codex share) and its holder (Opus.Brain.Wire, Elixir), over a `run` session of the backends service, each way one JSON object per line. A line is at most `max_line_bytes` bytes, UTF-8, the object's members exactly those its message names in `fields` (each present) and `optional` (each present or absent), each of the type `types` names: `id` a non-empty string of at most `max_id_bytes` bytes; `string` any string; `count` a whole number from 0; `boolean`; `object` a JSON object; `ids` and `strings` arrays of ids and of strings; `content` an array of blocks, each one `blocks` shows; `tools` an array of tools, each `{name, description, parameters}` with a name of 1 to 128 bytes, a description string and parameters an object; `config` an object of the members `config` names, each of its type; `counts` an object of exactly the four `counts` names, each a count; `model_counts` an array of `{model, counts}`, the model an id and the counts `counts`; `models` an array of `{id, name}`, both strings, the id an id; `phase` one of `phases`; `error_type` one of `error_types`; `accounting` one of `accountings`; `stop` one of `stops`. A list holds at most `max_list` entries. A line that does not read so, names a `t` the other side does not take, or is past a bound, ends the session: `refuse` gives such lines, each with its reason, and `read` gives lines that read, each with what it reads as. Commands go from the holder to the driver, events from the driver to the holder. The driver's first line is `hello`, naming the version and its `boot`, fresh for each driver process; the holder ends a session whose `hello` names another version, so a driver that does not know a member of this one is never written to. A `start`'s `config.read_only`, absent meaning false, starts the harness in its own read-only mode: Claude Code with only its own reading tools (Read, Grep, Glob), in its default permission mode, loading no settings file of the user's or the project's, every permission ask of its own tools denied, and a `permission_mode` or `harness_tools` beside it, or a row command carrying arguments of the harness's own, ends the driver; Codex's read-only sandbox cannot start in the box, so a read-only start ends Codex's driver before anything starts. With `read_only` false or absent a driver starts as it would without it. A delivery (`work`, `post`, `answer`) names the id the holder stored it under; `models` and `forget` an id the holder chose. The driver answers each command once: `start` with `started` or `gone`, `work`, `post` and `answer` with `accepted` once the harness's input took it or `refused` when it was not written, `models` with `models` or `refused`, `forget` with `forgot` or `refused`; the holder writes the next command only once the last is answered. `accepted` says the harness's pipe took the command and is not durable delivery: a post Codex accepted and then lost with its process can be missing from its transcript. `forgot` says the session's transcript and whatever holds its content are gone, each removed or proved absent; a diagnostic line of the harness's that names only the removed session's id may remain. A `start`'s `tools` are the tools a new native session starts with, for a harness whose session keeps the tools it started with for its life (Codex: a resume keeps the thread's own and a `work` changes none of them, so a tool a later work adds is not one the harness can call, and an ask of one the work lacks is still the holder's to refuse); a harness that takes each work's tools (Claude Code) takes them from the `work` and none from the start. Every event of a native turn (`text`, `said`, `own`, `ask`, `usage`, `idle`, `error`) names the `gen` its session was started with and, when the driver knows it, the `work` of the command whose line started that native turn; a native turn no command started (a background command's end) names none, and every one of those events may come so. `native` names those events: the program's own lines, which the driver writes only when its harness wrote one; the rest are the driver's own. `usage` names a native `result` (Claude Code: each result's own identity, which gives no order, so nothing compares two of them; its counts the result's alone) or a cumulative `total` per native thread (Codex: the thread's id, its one entry in `models` the thread's counts so far across every model it ran, under the model it runs now; totals are compared by native thread across model changes and boots, the model a total names never makes a baseline of its own, and a total below the last is a reset; a resume may repeat the last total with no `work`, which against an unchanged baseline adds no spend, and an increase no work can be given stays unattributed), exactly one of the two, and its `accounting`: `complete`, every model's counts the harness reports for it, side requests included, each counted once, in `models`; `partial`, the models whose counts read, some did not, or (Codex) every total of the session from the first line of a thread not the session's (a sub-agent's, which the driver does not pass on) or the session's own call of a sub-agent, since whether a thread's total holds its sub-agents' counts is not established, and (Codex) a resumed session's first usable total, one that carries counts, which may end a stretch a sub-agent worked in whose total's event never committed, since the driver keeps nothing across processes; `unavailable`, the harness reported none, and `models` is absent, never zeros. `models` is present exactly when the accounting is not `unavailable`. A `post`'s input to the harness carries a uuid derived from the post's id (Claude Code: its user line's `uuid`; Codex: its `clientUserMessageId`), so a result or a native turn naming the uuid names the post: the uuid is the first 16 bytes of the SHA-256 of `uuid.prefix` followed by the id, with the version nibble set to 4 and the variant bits to 10, written in lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 form; `uuid.cases` gives ids and their uuids. A `start` that resumes names in `pending` the posts whose delivery is not known, and `started.held` names those of them the session's transcript holds: delivery evidence and no more, since a post in the transcript may never have been answered; a pending post it leaves out is not established, never proved absent. A resume replays nothing but, for Codex, the thread's last total, and goes on with nothing by itself. There is no interrupt: Stop closes the session.
